The year was 1975 and I was in a band. We had been signed by a major label and we did a tour down the East Coast, across part of the south, and finished in LA. In LA, we got our advance for our album, paid for our tour, and had even managed to sell some merchandise, except we sold less merchandise than the label bought so we didn't actually make any money on that.

We were just young kids and the eldest was just 18. Our name was The Godlings which, in retrospect, was a horrible name. Frankly, we were immature and our music wasn't even very good. But, the big labels were signing up any acts that came their way who had a rebellious spirit and a punkish sound. We were somewhere between early punk and, I hate to admit this, acid rock.

Which is to say, we were horrible and they had no business signing us, but sign us they did!

In 1975, $25,000 was a lot of money. They gave each of us that as an advance on our record sales and something like another $18,000 each for our tour, less expenses, on our way out there. If you don't know, the labels will fuck you. In this case, we fucked them.

Pretty much immediately, we threw a giant party, complete with strippers, cocaine, heroin, beer, weed, more hookers, and trashed the rented house. We trashed the house so badly, we were evicted. I think we lived there for a week and a half, which was a hazy time and I'm pretty sure we violated every minor law on the books.

So, we all rented our own houses or apartments. This was great, we could party everywhere!

Wait, no... This was horrible - we partied everywhere. I don't recall going to the studio, not even once. In fact, I'm pretty sure we never went to the studio. It wasn't long before several of us showed signs of addiction and we were out of money. I think it might have been six months. I think the average salary back then was like $8,000 per year.

By the time we were done, it had pretty much turned into Young's song - Needle and the Damage Done.

"I caught you knocking at my cellar door, I love you baby can I have some more."

"I went to LA and I lost my band, I watched the needle take another man."

Now, I want to go back to my point about them signing us. They'd have never let us make an album. I don't actually know what they were thinking? We didn't seek them out, they sought us out. There's no way in hell they'd have let us make an album.

I don't like to use the word 'famous' but our most well known song was not fit for radio. There isn't even a way to make it fit for the radio.
